headline: Sage-A1.5 tests learned orchestration and verification in a 35B open-weight agent model
summary: Shanghai AI Laboratory describes Sage-A1.5 as a Mixture-of-Experts agent model with 35B total and 3B active parameters whose paper describes learned task orchestration and iterative evidence checking for long-horizon work. The authors report that enabling orchestration raises BrowseComp from 81.7 to 82.8 and DeepResearch-Bench II from 43.7 to 47.5, while broader comparisons are mixed. Model weights are available under Apache-2.0. The results are author-reported, and independent reproduction, external deployment performance, and total inference cost remain open. In one scientist-guided computational-chemistry workflow, the authors report about 12 hours of agent execution versus an estimated human work-week; that human-time estimate is not a matched measurement. The paper depicts quantized local deployment, but reports no matched hardware speed or cost result.
